mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the 3-month change in FEDFUNDS being negative) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in declining FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes economic slowdown and triggers risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC between UNRATE crossing 4.5% and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL MoM > 0.3%) and stagnant or falling interest rates (FEDFUNDS <= 4.0%) indicates a delayed monetary policy response to inflation, which increases real interest rate uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL MoM > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS <= 4.0%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC between the interaction signal and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a monthly decline in housing starts exceeding 0.5% signals a weakening in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, when HOUST declines > 0.5% MoM, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC between the HOUST decline signal and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (measured as the 3-month change in PAYEMS being positive) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in periods of PAYEMS growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (the 2017 base index) indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, which typically precedes economic slowdown and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC between INDPRO falling below 100 and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts (HOUST MoM > 0.5%) and declining industrial production (INDPRO MoM < -0.3%) indicates a sectoral imbalance where demand is strong in housing but supply is weak in manufacturing, which often precedes economic uncertainty and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST MoM > 0.5% and INDPRO MoM < -0.3%, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC between the interaction signal and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%), a monetary policy tightening (FEDFUNDS MoM rise > 0.25%) signals the Fed's commitment to combat inflation, which increases uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS MoM rise > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%
failure_condition: In high-inflation periods (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%), when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% MoM, the S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC between the FEDFUNDS rise signal and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
